sentences.text:
THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

In this appeal, the appellant has challenged the judgment dated 01.10.2014 in M.V.C.No.5122/2011 passed by the Court of Small Causes and M.A.C.T., Bangalore (SCCH-09) ('the Tribunal' in short) in dismissing the claim petition claimed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1989.

entities.text: Court of Small Causes and M.A.C.T., Bangalore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are, on 13.05.2011 in between 01:30 - 01:45 pm, the petitioner has met with an accident while riding the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04/EA-7387 as pillion rider, which was skid and caused him the injuries.

After taking treatment, he has moved the Tribunal seeking NC:
2023:KHC:34390 compensation of Rs.25,00,000/-.
Claim was opposed by the respondents denying the very accident.
After taking evidence, the Tribunal by impugned judgment doubted the occurrence of accident and dismissed the claim petition.
Aggrieved by the same, the petitioner has filed this appeal on various grounds.

4. Heard the arguments of Sri. T.N. Viswanatha, learned counsel for the petitioner, Sri. R.
Shashidhara, learned counsel for respondents No.1 and 2 and Sri. Kishore Kumar Reddy, learned counsel for the Insurance Company.
5.

It is the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner was the pillion rider of the vehicle and for the reason that respondent No.2/rider of the vehicle has rode the vehicle negligently, the motor cycle was skidded on Bengaluru-Tumkur road near CMTI, Yeswanthapur,
Bengaluru causing him the injuries.

The petitioner NC: 2023:KHC:34390 was treated at M.S.
Ramaiah Hospital, Bengaluru, underwent surgery and for this reason, he could not able to file the complaint.
The 2nd respondent being the rider himself has registered a complaint in C.Misc.No.188/2011.
The petitioner has placed all material evidence in proof of the accident, but the Tribunal erroneously doubted the accident and dismissed the claim and sought for interference.

6. Per contra, learned counsel for respondents No.1 and 2 has contended that respondent No.2 being the rider has reported the accident to the Police, instead of registering a criminal case, C.Misc. case has been registered.
The scooter was insured with respondent No.3 also covers the risk of the petitioner, respondent No.2 is holding valid driving licence and there are no objection for the assessment of compensation.

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for the Insurance Company has contended that the accident has not been NC:
2023:KHC:34390 proved, the petitioner has not placed any evidence that he has sustained injury in the accident.
The investigation made by the Insurance Company clearly points out that the petitioner was the rider of the motor cycle by himself and due to his negligence, fall from the bike.
There is no accident, 2nd respondent has not caused any accident and self- fall from the motor cycle has been converted into an accident for the sake of compensation.

The Tribunal after considering the medical evidence, recorded its finding that the accident is not believable, so also the injury sustained by the petitioner and rightly dismissed the claim petition and he supported the impugned judgment.
8. I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on both the sides and also perused the materials on record.

9. The petitioner has approached the Tribunal on the ground that he was met with an accident on NC: 2023:KHC:34390 13.05.2011 between 01:30 - 01:45 pm at Benglaluru-Tumkur road being the pillion rider.
The same is also the evidence placed before the Tribunal.
The material on record did point out that when the petitioner was brought to the hospital, history was furnished as skid and fall from the two-wheeler.
The details of the vehicle, rider of the motor cycle, petitioner as pillion rider are not revealed.
In order to establish the accident, the petitioner requires to prove the accident.
He has to establish the injury sustained on account of the accident.
10. The contention of the Insurance Company that the petitioner himself was the rider is accepted by the Tribunal.
In order to prove the accident, except self-serving testimony of the petitioner, there are no independence evidence.
Ex.P1 is the copy of the complaint under which C.Misc. has been registered.
Ex.P1 is not the complaint lodged to the Police by the petitioner.
It is the complaint filed by NC: 2023:KHC:34390 the respondent No.2 reporting about the accident.
The recitals of Ex.P1 explains, at the place of accident, due to Metro work, the motor cycle was skidded and the petitioner had sustained fracture of femur and admitted to M.S. Ramaiah Hospital.
If really the petitioner has met with an accident, he ought to have filed the complaint to the Police, but admittedly there is no complaint.
The hospital records pertains to M.S. Ramaiah Hospital speaks that the petitioner sustained the injuries on 13.03.2011 at about 01:30 pm at Goraguntepalya due to skid and fall.
There is no criminal prosecution against the respondent No.2.
The evidence placed before the Tribunal in proof of the accident is not suffice.
Mere non
-filing of FIR, non-prosecution of respondent No.2 is not a ground to doubt the genuineness of the accident.
The petitioner has sustained fracture of femur in the said accident.
Whether he was pillion rider or rider of the motor cycle, proper evidence is required to be placed NC: 2023:KHC:34390 before the Tribunal.
Due to lack of evidence, the Tribunal could decide that there is no accident.
An opportunity has to be provided to the petitioner to establish these aspects.
The petitioners can explain skid and fall from the two-wheeler as noted in Ex.R1.
He is required to examine eye witness of the accident, person who recorded the history of the accident, treated doctor and the police officer who registered the C.Misc. case.
Hence, it is a fit case which warrants remand to consider the case afresh by giving an opportunity to the petitioner to lead further evidence to prove the accident.

In the result, the following:

sentences.text: i) The appeal is allowed.
ii) Impugned judgment is set aside.
iii) The claim petition is restored to the stage of leading further evidence.

iv) The Tribunal is requested to give an opportunity to the petitioner to lead further NC: 2023:KHC:34390 evidence in order to prove the accident, injury sustained by him, who was the rider of the motor cycle and to decide the case afresh in accordance with law.
v) Without further notice, parties to appear before the Tribunal on 03.10.2023.
